item.text: I’ll refactor the hooks across both operations so an `Ok` from a hook only permits the native action; it can’t stand in for writing, syncing, checked close, rename, link, or temp removal. I’ll preserve the existing injected error/race coverage and add explicit no-op-hook success tests for both commit paths.

I’m continuing the r2 review repair. I’ll first check the current hook call sites and dirty overlay, then make the smallest cohesive change so every successful hook still leads to the required native operation.

The hook interfaces are now gates: they can inject errors or choose a short-write limit, but successful returns flow into the native write, sync, checked close, rename/link, unlink, and directory sync. I’m adapting the existing scripted failure cases to that contract and adding successful-hook assertions against real filesystem effects.
